newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher, funds buy 30 mln bushels.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher, funds buy 30 mln bushels.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher, supported by USDA export sales figures which came in above expectations and aggressive fund buying totaling at least 30 million bushels, traders said.
"Everybody says it's going to slow down (exports) but so far it's not slowing down. Exports were good for everything," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans during the week ended March 13 totaled 428,400 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes. Japan and Taiwan were the major buyers, USDA said.
Domestic usage was also running strong. The U.S. Census February report showed soybean crushings during the month of February were at 125.152 million bushels.

"The February crush number was strong," said Allen Dever, soybean market analyst with Doane Agriculture Services. "The crush is running at a seasonally adjusted pace of 1.564 billion bushels. USDA put it at 1.42 billion. Clearly we're running at a pace we cannot sustain or we'll run out of soybeans."
Soybeans closed 13 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher with May up 13 at $8.52 a bushel.

Taiwan's pork export halt due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease could lead to a 20 percent drop in that country's corn imports, Taiwan grain buyers said. CBOT floor sources said soybean and soymeal exports could also taper off.

Funds again were aggressive buyers of soybeans, accounting for at least 30 million bushels. But gains were pared late as soymeal futures slipped. Traders said soymeal basis levels in Brazil fell on Thursday, prompting crushers to sell.
"The Brazilian nearby meal basis is breaking," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
On the day, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer bought at least 10 million bushels May, Refco Inc bought 6.5 million May and Griffin Trading bought six million July, traders said.
Lind-Waldock spread three million July/May and ADM spread 1.5 million May/July.
In options trade, Refco Inc bought 600 May $7.75 puts at four cents and Produce Grain sold 100 July $9.50 calls and 100 July $10.00 calls at 20 to 27-1/2 cents.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 82,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 46,843 contracts.
